scenario: The planner receives a complete feature description and writes a plan.
failureMode: The planner writes an unstructured plan or changes project code.

scenario: A material requirement is missing or ambiguous.
failureMode: The planner silently invents a missing technical requirement.

scenario: The slugified plan path already exists under the selected CBM index.
failureMode: An update creates a duplicate plan instead of modifying the selected record.

scenario: The planner receives duplicate items, an exact KEEP token, or a malformed candidate update.
failureMode: A malformed candidate overwrites a valid plan or leaks interactive transcript state.

scenario: The planner materializes ordered construction steps that must be resumed and audited independently.

assertions.expected: Each ordered step starts with its own [ ] checkbox

failureMode: The planner emits one aggregate status row or a legend without a checkbox on each ordered item.

scenario: A candidate plan contains a status legend but one ordered step lacks its own checkbox.
failureMode: AIDX must infer item state from an aggregate receipt or prose instead of reading the item directly.

scenario: A plan changes a skill package and must give AIDX an explicit owner step.
failureMode: The planner leaves skill ownership implicit and AIDX edits a skill package directly.

scenario: A plan changes a non-skill project file and must not invent an unrelated skill-manager step.
failureMode: The planner adds an unconditional owner step that obscures the actual ordered work.

scenario: The planner researches a domain-specific example package and must strengthen the reusable planning workflow.
failureMode: The plan copies domain entities, feature names, field values, or implementation details into the reusable AIDP contract.

scenario: A researched example contains useful workflow controls mixed with domain-specific implementation details.
failureMode: The planner treats an example artifact as a template and leaks its business vocabulary into the reusable plan.

scenario: The planner decomposes a multi-file change for an executor with no prior context.
failureMode: The plan names broad work but leaves file ownership, interfaces, and test boundaries for AIDX to rediscover.

scenario: The draft plan contains vague implementation language or unverified cross-step names.
failureMode: AIDX receives TODO-level instructions or a plan whose requirements and interfaces were never checked by AIDP.

scenario: A plan must begin from repository evidence before decomposing work across different languages and project layouts.
failureMode: The planner guesses the repository structure, commands, or target classification from filenames and hands discovery back to AIDX.

scenario: A refactor request must preserve behavior while making scope, alternatives, coverage, and safe increments explicit.
failureMode: The planner treats refactoring as unrestricted cleanup or leaves behavior preservation, test gaps, and sequencing for AIDX to infer.

scenario: A plan targets a repository with an observed language or framework and must apply only relevant shared guidance and project gates.
failureMode: The planner copies generic language rules, guesses the stack, or invents a universal test command instead of mapping observed language risks to project-owned proof.

scenario: The planner must select a supported create or same-slug update operation without probing unsupported flags.
failureMode: The planner guesses command variants or repeats failed invocations because the supported operation and argument contract are not documented.

scenario: An existing plan needs one section or list item added or replaced while generated context and retained items must remain stable.

assertions.expected: Add or append a section item

failureMode: The update duplicates generated context, drops retained list items, or sends unsupported section flags to the materializer.

scenario: The planner must collect a list with fewer prompt round trips while preventing an oversized or ambiguous answer from being accepted.

assertions.expected: never issue one prompt per item

failureMode: The planner asks once per list item, accepts unreliable pseudo-batches, or silently continues after malformed or oversized input.

scenario: A request asks for implementation, but the authoring lane's restrictions are present in the draft plan content.

assertions.expected: AIDP authoring controls belong in this skill

failureMode: AIDP leaks its own planning-only restrictions into the executable plan and creates a contradiction for AIDX.

scenario: A candidate contains both an AIDP-only no-implementation control and an AIDX implementation handoff.
failureMode: The materializer accepts a contradictory plan and leaves the executor to resolve an authoring-versus-execution conflict.

scenario: AIDP exposes the shared six-part skill contract with its own planning boundaries.
failureMode: The skill omits a shared contract slot, leaving its inputs, ordering, proof, or boundaries implicit.

scenario: AIDP keeps the adapted contract compatible with uncertainty and interactive clarification.
failureMode: A reusable skill is forced into a provider-specific exact-output persona that conflicts with its actual planning contract.
